NKJV.1: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD, and spoke, saying: “I will sing to the LORD, For He has triumphed gloriously! The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea!
NKJV.2: The LORD is my strength and song, And He has become my salvation; He is my God, and I will praise Him; My father’s God, and I will exalt Him.
NKJV.3: The LORD is a man of war; The LORD is His name.
NKJV.4: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army He has cast into the sea;  His chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea.
NKJV.5: The depths have covered them;  They sank to the bottom like a stone.
NKJV.6: “Your right hand, O LORD, has become glorious in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has dashed the enemy in pieces.
NKJV.7: And in the greatness of Your excellence You have overthrown those who rose against You; You sent forth Your wrath; It consumed them like stubble.
NKJV.8: And with the blast of Your nostrils The waters were gathered together;  The floods stood upright like a heap; The depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
NKJV.9: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; My desire shall be satisfied on them. I will draw my sword, My hand shall destroy them.’
NKJV.10: You blew with Your wind, The sea covered them; They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
NKJV.11: “Who is like You, O LORD, among the gods? Who is like You, glorious in holiness, Fearful in praises, doing wonders?
NKJV.12: You stretched out Your right hand; The earth swallowed them.
NKJV.13: You in Your mercy have led forth The people whom You have redeemed; You have guided them in Your strength To Your holy habitation.
NKJV.14: “The people will hear and be afraid; Sorrow will take hold of the inhabitants of Philistia.
NKJV.15: Then the chiefs of Edom will be dismayed;  The mighty men of Moab, Trembling will take hold of them;  All the inhabitants of Canaan will melt away.
NKJV.16: Fear and dread will fall on them; By the greatness of Your arm They will be as still as a stone, Till Your people pass over, O LORD, Till the people pass over Whom You have purchased.
NKJV.17: You will bring them in and plant them In the mountain of Your inheritance, In the place, O LORD, which You have made For Your own dwelling, The sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established.
NKJV.18: “The  LORD shall reign forever and ever.”
NKJV.19: For the horses of Pharaoh went with his chariots and his horsemen into the sea, and the LORD brought back the waters of the sea upon them. But the children of Israel went on dry land in the midst of the sea.
NKJV.20: Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.
NKJV.21: And Miriam answered them:  “Sing to the LORD, For He has triumphed gloriously! The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea!”
NKJV.22: So Moses brought Israel from the Red Sea; then they went out into the Wilderness of Shur. And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water.
NKJV.23: Now when they came to Marah, they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter. Therefore the name of it was called Marah.
NKJV.24: And the people complained against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”
NKJV.25: So he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree. When he cast it into the waters, the waters were made sweet. There He made a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them,
NKJV.26: and said, “If you diligently heed the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in His sight, give ear to His commandments and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have brought on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
NKJV.27: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve wells of water and seventy palm trees; so they camped there by the waters.

NASB.1: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to the LORD, and said, 'I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; The horse and its rider He has hurled into the sea.
NASB.2: 'The LORD is my strength and song, And He has become my salvation; This is my God, and I will praise Him; My father's God, and I will extol Him.
NASB.3: 'The LORD is a warrior; The LORD is His name.
NASB.4: 'Pharaoh's chariots and his army He has cast into the sea; And the choicest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
NASB.5: 'The deeps cover them; They went down into the depths like a stone.
NASB.6: 'Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power, Your right hand, O LORD, shatters the enemy.
NASB.7: 'And in the greatness of Your excellence You overthrow those who rise up against You; You send forth Your burning anger, [and] it consumes them as chaff.
NASB.8: 'At the blast of Your nostrils the waters were piled up, The flowing waters stood up like a heap; The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea.
NASB.9: 'The enemy said, 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; My desire shall be gratified against them; I will draw out my sword, my hand will destroy them.'
NASB.10: 'You blew with Your wind, the sea covered them; They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
NASB.11: 'Who is like You among the gods, O LORD? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, Awesome in praises, working wonders?
NASB.12: 'You stretched out Your right hand, The earth swallowed them.
NASB.13: 'In Your lovingkindness You have led the people whom You have redeemed; In Your strength You have guided [them] to Your holy habitation.
NASB.14: 'The peoples have heard, they tremble; Anguish has gripped the inhabitants of Philistia.
NASB.15: 'Then the chiefs of Edom were dismayed; The leaders of Moab, trembling grips them; All the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away.
NASB.16: 'Terror and dread fall upon them; By the greatness of Your arm they are motionless as stone; Until Your people pass over, O LORD, Until the people pass over whom You have purchased.
NASB.17: 'You will bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, The place, O LORD, which You have made for Your dwelling, The sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established.
NASB.18: 'The LORD shall reign forever and ever.'
NASB.19: For the horses of Pharaoh with his chariots and his horsemen went into the sea, and the LORD brought back the waters of the sea on them, but the sons of Israel walked on dry land through the midst of the sea.
NASB.20: Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took the timbrel in her hand, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dancing.
NASB.21: Miriam answered them, 'Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; The horse and his rider He has hurled into the sea.'
NASB.22: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness and found no water.
NASB.23: When they came to Marah, they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter; therefore it was named Marah.
NASB.24: So the people grumbled at Moses, saying, 'What shall we drink?'
NASB.25: Then he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree; and he threw [it] into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There He made for them a statute and regulation, and there He tested them.
NASB.26: And He said, 'If you will give earnest heed to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His sight, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I, the LORD, am your healer.'
NASB.27: Then they came to Elim where there [were] twelve springs of water and seventy date palms, and they camped there beside the waters.

NLT.1:
Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD,
for he has triumphed gloriously;
he has hurled both horse and rider
into the sea.
NLT.2:
The LORD is my strength and my song;
he has given me victory.
This is my God, and I will praise him —
my father’s God, and I will exalt him!
NLT.3:
The LORD is a warrior;
Yahweh is his name!
NLT.4:
Pharaoh’s chariots and army
he has hurled into the sea.
The finest of Pharaoh’s officers
are drowned in the Red Sea.
NLT.5:
The deep waters gushed over them;
they sank to the bottom like a stone.
NLT.6:
“Your right hand, O LORD,
is glorious in power.
Your right hand, O LORD,
smashes the enemy.
NLT.7:
In the greatness of your majesty,
you overthrow those who rise against you.
You unleash your blazing fury;
it consumes them like straw.
NLT.8:
At the blast of your breath,
the waters piled up!
The surging waters stood straight like a wall;
in the heart of the sea the deep waters became hard.
NLT.9:
“The enemy boasted, ‘I will chase them
and catch up with them.
I will plunder them
and consume them.
I will flash my sword;
my powerful hand will destroy them.’
NLT.10:
But you blew with your breath,
and the sea covered them.
They sank like lead
in the mighty waters.
NLT.11:
“Who is like you among the gods, O LORD —
glorious in holiness,
awesome in splendor,
performing great wonders?
NLT.12:
You raised your right hand,
and the earth swallowed our enemies.
NLT.13:
“With your unfailing love you lead
the people you have redeemed.
In your might, you guide them
to your sacred home.
NLT.14:
The peoples hear and tremble;
anguish grips those who live in Philistia.
NLT.15:
The leaders of Edom are terrified;
the nobles of Moab tremble.
All who live in Canaan melt away;
NLT.16:
terror and dread fall upon them.
The power of your arm
makes them lifeless as stone
until your people pass by, O LORD,
until the people you purchased pass by.
NLT.17:
You will bring them in and plant them on your own mountain —
